Liverpool spent close to £400m on Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz and Bradley Barcola. Against Brentford, there was evidence that expensively-assembled attack might finally be clicking. Isak was on the fringes of the game for long periods, limited to only 16 touches by the dogged hosts. But his brilliantly-taken goal, controlled and rifled home with dizzying speed in the second half, was a reminder of just how deadly he can be at his best. It took him to five goals for the season. Only Erling Haaland has scored more in the Premier League. He is putting a difficult first season behind him and Andoni Iraola will be encouraged that it was Barcola who provided the assist. metadata.summary: Britain's Sonay Kartal says making her maiden WTA 1000 final at the Wuhan Open is a "dream come true," adding that the mental side of sport is "one of my strongest assets."

Kartal became only the second British woman, after Johanna Konta (Beijing 2016, Miami 2017, Rome 2019), to reach a WTA 1000 final with a stunning 7-6 (11-9) 7-6 (7-5) victory over Jelena Ostapenko. The 24-year-old, playing in only her third tournament since returning from a back injury, saved multiple set points to punish Ostapenko, despite the Latvian hitting an astonishing 50 winners in the match. Brentford head coach Keith Andrews felt Jeremy Jacquet was "cute and clever" for his role in Yehor Yarmoliuk's red card in the 2-1 defeat to Liverpool. Ukraine international Yarmoliuk was sent off in the eighth minute of first-half stoppage time at the Gtech Community Stadium for catching Jacquet with what referee John Brooks called - after going to the VAR monitor - "a headbutting action". messages.text: Ombudsman simply supreme in Champion Stakes

metadata.summary: Ombudsman exacted Qatar Racing Champion Stakes revenge on Calandagan to come out on top with a show-stopping performance at Ascot.
metadata.content: Ascot: Ombudsman simply supreme in Champion Stakes for Gosden team | Racing News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Ascot: Ombudsman simply supreme in Champion Stakes for Gosden team Ombudsman reversed the form with last year's winner Calandagan in the latest renewal of the Qatar Racing Champion Stakes at Ascot under William Buick; result was one of three successes on the day for owners Godolphin, who also claimed the QEII and Balmoral Handicap Saturday 17 October 2026 17:06, UK Image: Ombudsman won the Champion Stakes Ombudsman exacted Qatar Racing Champion Stakes revenge on Calandagan to come out on top with a show-stopping performance at Ascot. It was Francis-Henri Graffard's French raider who took home the spoils 12 months ago, but this time around there was a decisive verdict in favour of John and Thady Gosden's home favourite, who obliged as the 5-4 market leader. With the six-strong field heading into the home straight grouped tightly, the stage was set for Ombudsman to demonstrate the blistering turn of foot that has often been a hallmark of his career. When William Buick asked him to quicken, he scorched past eventual third Bay City Roller before seeing off Calandagan to banish Juddmonte International disappointment and prove he is truly one of the best middle-distance horses on the planet.
